knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 5.1.7
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly distinguishes the Bayesian credibility approach in simple cases and names the premium object calculated?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Bayesian approach treats structural parameters as known from prior structure. Empirical Bayes estimates them from data, a different approach.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Explicit prior structure supplies mu and Z; premium Z X̄ + (1-Z) mu.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Collapsing Bayesian credibility into Empirical Bayes.

choices.label: Bayesian credibility uses an explicit prior or structural distribution for risk parameters. The premium object is Z times X̄ + (1 minus Z) times μ with Z and mu determined theoretically from the prior structure in simple cases.
Applying Bayesian credibility finishes the Empirical Bayes approach because both yield a numeric premium.
Bayesian credibility never supplies mu or Z; only Empirical Bayes defines those quantities.
The premium object is the posterior mean only; Z and mu never appear in Bayesian credibility.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 5.1.7
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. In a simple Bayesian credibility setup with known structural parameters, the credibility premium takes the form Z times X̄ + (1 minus Z) times μ. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: State what prior supplies; refuse EB conflation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Known structural parameters from prior theory yield mu and Z. EB estimates structural parameters from collective experience.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Prior supplies mean and variance components for mu and Z. EB estimates structurals from data.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Accepting Bayesian credibility as finishing Empirical Bayes.

choices.label: The prior or known structural distribution supplies the overall mean and variance components so mu and Z are determined theoretically, then combined with observed X̄. Empirical Bayes estimates those structural parameters from data; a different approach from treating them as known in the Bayesian calculation.
Applying Bayesian credibility finishes the Empirical Bayes approach.
mu and Z must be estimated from collective data even in the fully Bayesian setup; prior structure supplies nothing.
Structural parameters are always user-chosen constants unrelated to any prior; Z equals 1 by definition.

worked_example.title: Bühlmann Z from prior structure, then premium
worked_example.problem_statement: In a Bayesian credibility (Bühlmann) setting, the expected process variance is EVPV = 120 and the variance of hypothetical means is VHM = 40, so k = EVPV/VHM = 3. A risk has n = 6 observation years with X̄ = £850. The prior mean of the hypothetical means is μ = £700. Compute Z = n/(n+k) and the credibility premium.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Confirm k = 120/40, then Z = n/(n+k), then P = Z X̄ + (1 − Z)μ.

steps.label: Confirm k from prior structure
steps.explanation: The Bayesian approach supplies structural parameters (including μ and k) from an explicit prior/process model.

steps.label: Credibility factor
steps.explanation: More years of data increase Z toward 1.

steps.label: Credibility premium
steps.explanation: The premium blends experience with the prior mean μ.

worked_example.common_pitfall: Using Z = k/(n+k) = 1/3 (the weight on μ) as if it were the credibility factor on X̄, which swaps the blend to £750.
